title: [YouPass Collect] - Urban population growth: 1950, 2000 & 2030
prompt: The chart below gives information about the growth of the urban population in certain parts of the world, including the prediction of the future. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the proportion of urban population in four regions of the world, namely Africa, Asia, Latin America and the entire world, in 1950, 2000, and 2030, with the last year being a projection.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all four regions experienced or are expected to experience an upward trend in urbanization over the 80-year period. Throughout this time, Latin America consistently had the highest percentage of city dwellers, while Africa and Asia recorded considerably lower figures.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding regions with higher urbanization rates, in 1950, Latin America led with 42% of its population residing in urban areas, compared to 30% for the global average. By 2000, the former had risen substantially to 70%, and this figure is projected to reach 80% by 2030. Similar changes can be seen in the figure for the worldwide urban population, which increased to 48% in 2000 and is expected to continue climbing to 60% at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for Africa and Asia, both regions started with nearly identical urbanization levels in 1950, at 12% and 14%, in that order. Over the following five decades, these figures saw similar increases, with both significantly rising to 39% in 2000. By 2030, Asia's urban population is predicted to reach 56%, slightly higher than Africa's projected figure of 51%.
